entry.title: 'People are still afraid of those three letters': Fighting the stigma of HIV
entry.summary: That's a quote from former rugby star Gareth Thomas, who is HIV positive. At the International AIDS Conference in Rio this year, he spoke out about the isolation and discrimination tied to the virus.

entry.title: A cancer survivor hoped to work — then she lost her Medicaid disability coverage
entry.summary: As state governments grapple with how to determine who's sick enough to be excused from new Medicaid work requirements, some families are already struggling with what illnesses guarantee health coverage because of a disability.

entry.title: As diseases loom, CDC's response to measles deaths stirs fears about agency's reliability
entry.summary: The worst U.S. measles outbreak in decades is growing and flu season is imminent. Experts are fretting about federal health data reliability after the CDC questioned two Pennsylvania measles deaths.

entry.title: 'I've never seen anything like this' -- A U.S. doctor treats Ebola's youngest victims
entry.summary: Dr. Rupa Narra is a U.S. pediatrician who arrived in the Democratic Republic of Congo to help care for stricken children. Nothing could have prepared her for what she'd face.

entry.title: Special education head at Education Department abruptly resigns
entry.summary: The leader of the Education Department's special education office told employees she is resigning after less than four months in the role and as the agency overall is morphing and shrinking.

entry.title: Whatever happened to the measles outbreak that shocked a country this year?
entry.summary: Bangladesh has seen over 50,000 confirmed or suspected cases of measles this year. The death toll among children just surpassed 1,000. How are officials trying to bring the outbreak under control?

entry.title: How to fight with the people we care about, illustrated
entry.summary: Arguing with a partner or a loved one can be anxiety-inducing. Conflict resolution facilitator Priya Parker explains how to start and end a fight — while easing dread for everyone.

entry.title: A Louisiana case could upend telehealth abortion. What exactly is it?
entry.summary: As a federal appeals court considers Louisiana's lawsuit to end telehealth abortion access, a longtime OB-GYN in Arizona explains how telehealth works in his clinic.

entry.title: Whatever happened to the Taliban threat: 'We will flog the women'?
entry.summary: In 2024, the ruling Taliban pledged to use flogging as well as stoning to punish people for not following certain of their precepts — committing adultery, running secret schools for girls. Have they followed through?

entry.title: One rural hospital offers hope amid nationwide rural maternity ward closures
entry.summary: As more rural hospitals shut down maternity wards, one hospital in Minnesota has a survival strategy that could spur others to imitate it.
